content: We need to find template that when applied to target molecule (the ketone) reproduces the Wolff-Kishner reduction: ketone -> alkane. The target molecule is the ketone? Input from previous step: make_8_lvl2-apply_template-4 had answer [] meaning applying some template gave no precursors. We need to find template that when applied to the molecule below reproduces the reaction: fully reducing a ketone into an alkane. The molecule below? Not given explicitly but likely the ketone substrate. Probably "CC(=O)C" (propanone) as used. The retrosynthetic step: target alkane "CCC" from ketone "CC(=O)C". So we need a template that when applied to "CC(=O)C" gives precursor "CCC". Actually retrosynthesis: product is alkane, precursors include ketone and hydrazine etc. But they ask for mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule below, reproduces the reaction. The template should map ketone to alkane. We have applied template 62097 gave product "CCC(C)=O" which is not correct. Template 970 gave "CC(C)O". Not correct. Need template that transforms ketone to alkane. Search for templates where retro_smarts maybe [C:2]-[C:1]=[O]>>[C:2][C:1] (i.e., carbonyl to alkane). Let's search for functional_groups_broken "ketones" and functional_groups_formed maybe none. Already got many templates but none seem to do reduction. Look at template 62097 mapping: [CH3]-[C]=[O]>>C-[CH2]-[C]=[O] not reduction. Need template where forward reaction is reduction: carbonyl + hydrazine -> alkane? But retrosynthetic template would break C=O bond and add N? Actually retrosynthesis: target alkane, precursors include ketone. So template should be reverse of reduction: alkane -> ketone? Wait retrosynthetic step: we have product alkane, we want to go back to ketone (precursor). So applying template to alkane should give ketone. But they ask: "when applied to the molecule below (provided as available input data), reproduces the reaction". The molecule below likely the alkane? The input from make_8_lvl2-apply_template-4 had answer [] meaning applying some template to something gave no precursors. That step likely attempted to apply template to alkane and got none. So we need to find correct template that when applied to alkane yields ketone (i.e., reverse of reduction). The molecule below maybe "CCC". So we need template that transforms alkane to ketone. Search for templates where retro_smarts: [C:2]-[CH3]>>[C:2]=[O]?? Let's search for functional_groups_formed "ketones". Use search with functional_groups_formed = ["ketones"] and broken maybe none.
